title: The Immune System
text: The immune system is the complex network of cells, tissues, and organs that defends the body against pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites. It consists of innate immunity, which provides immediate nonspecific defenses, and adaptive immunity, which develops specific responses to pathogens over time. Key components include white blood cells (leukocytes), antibodies, and the lymphatic system. T cells and B cells are the primary cells of adaptive immunity; B cells produce antibodies, while T cells directly kill infected cells or regulate immune responses. Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues.
